title: How to continue to maintain the presence of web console functionality when using the Java embedded API
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Hi, I am using the Java embedded API, and I want to continue using the functionality provided by the web console. What should I do. I want to use the web console as a database management tool

### Describe the solution you'd like.

_No response_

### Describe alternatives you've considered.

_No response_

### Additional context.

_No response_

comments.body: The `questDb.start(false);` is so that I control when I shutdown QuestDB, rather than when my app terminates.

CREATE TABLE tab AS (
    SELECT

        rnd_long() value,

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
hi!, I have been working on an issue and been keeping you in mind. In this PR https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/3183/files#diff-fac2030b90f1d9e80a597c778dad544393d8d1fe7885bff19ca89403009736b5

there is a new test class `core/src/test/java/io/questdb/test/ServerMainBackupDatabaseTest.java` that sort of exemplifies what you are doing (_testServerMainBackupDatabase_):

- create start QuestDB:
   
   ```java
   try (
       ServerMain qdb = new ServerMain("-d", rootDir, Bootstrap.SWITCH_USE_DEFAULT_LOG_FACTORY_CONFIGURATION);
       SqlCompiler defaultCompiler = new SqlCompiler(qdb.getCairoEngine());
       SqlExecutionContext defaultContext = executionContext(qdb.getCairoEngine())
   ) {
       qdb.start();
       ...
   } // QuestDB server ends here
   ```
   in this case we launch the server and it will close automatically. After `qdb.start()` the webconsole will be available.

- use the server as a framework. In the test I get the **engine** and I use it to create as many compilers as I need.

Notes:
- compilers are not thread safe, make sure only one thread at the time is using a given compiler.
- each compiler requires a context, so create a context every time you create a compiler.
- use each compiler, context as many times as you need.
- when you are done with the compilers, free them and their resources (a call to close will do).

In the test, we create a defaultCompiler for convenience, and N compilers because they will be used by N threads concurrently.

The test deals with backups, but if you look in the codebase for classes that are named `ServerMain...` you will find **ServerMainForeignTableTest** which creates tables concurrently.

Notes on dissapearing directories:
- WAL tables do generate ephemeral directories that are culled aynchronously when there are no readers for them.
- when you have readers on the table, any SQL that changes the table will version upwards all required partition folders and metadata files. For instance if you have partition 2023-04-20 and a reader is selecting on it, and at the same time there is an insert for that partition, or an update, or drop/detach, alter..., then all those changes will be done to a copy on write copy of 2023-04-20 which will be called 2023-04-20.1. When the select is over, QuestDB will remove 2023-04-20. 
- not only partition folders and metadata files are versioned, also the WAL metadata files. In the end, once a WAL has been applied, it can be removed.

If you notice that these directories' versions shoot up like bamboo, it means that you probaby have too high a granularity for the table (partition by) and perhaps if you lowered (YEAR -> MONTH, MONTH -> WEEK, ...) then there would be less collisions on write, there would be less overhead.
